title: BONN Dialysis renal and CARDiovascular disease biobank, BONDCARD
summary: The “BONDCARD” study at the University Hospital Bonn investigates why people with severe kidney disease who require dialysis are more likely to develop heart and blood vessel diseases. To do this, blood, urine, and, in patients receiving peritoneal dialysis, dialysate samples will be collected and analyzed regularly from 300 adult dialysis patients over a period of five years. The goal is to identify certain substances in the body that may help predict heart problems or worsening kidney function at an early stage. Researchers hope to better understand how conditions such as heart failure, irregular heart rhythms, vascular calcification, and heart valve disease develop in dialysis patients. The samples will be collected as part of routine dialysis treatment, meaning no additional burdensome procedures are required. In addition, patients will receive a yearly ECG and an ultrasound examination of the heart. If surplus tissue becomes available during medically necessary procedures, it may also be used for research purposes. All data and samples will be stored securely and treated confidentially. In the long term, the study aims to help identify high-risk patients earlier and improve the personalization of medical treatments.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Chronic kidney disease stage V
Treatment with hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of capacity to give informed consent
Insufficient knowledge of the German language, making consent without an interpreter impossible
